source_text: Firmilianus Cypriano fratri, in Domino salutem. Accepimus per Rogatianum charissimum nostrum diaconum a vobis missum litteras quas ad nos fecisti, frater dilectissime; et gratias propter hoc Domino maximas egimus quod contigerit ut qui corpore ab invicem separamur sic spiritu adunemur quasi non unam tantum regionem tenentes, sed in ipsa atque in eadem domo simul inhabitantes. Quod et decet dicere, quia et spiritalis domus Dei una est. Erit enim in novissimis, ait Propheta, diebus manifestus mons Domini et domus Dei super vertices montium. In quam convenientes cum jucunditate adunantur, secundum quod et in Psalmo hoc postulatur a Domino inhabitare in domo Dei per omnes dies vitae. Unde et in alio loco manifestatum est esse apud sanctos magnam voluntatis charitatem inunum convenire. Ecce, inquit, quam bonum et voluptabile est ut habitent fratres in unum!
pass_a_gloss: Firmilianus to Cyprian brother, in Lord greeting. We received through Rogatianus our most dear deacon sent by you letters which you made to us, most beloved brother; and thanks we gave to Lord greatest because of this that it happened that we who are separated from each other in body are thus united in spirit as if not holding just one region, but inhabiting at the same time in the same and in this house. Which also is fitting to say, because spiritual house of God is one. For in the last days, says Prophet, mountain of Lord and house of God will be manifest above tops of mountains. Into which gathering with joy they are united, according to which also in this Psalm it is asked of Lord to inhabit in house of God through all days of life. From which also in another place it has been made manifest that there is among saints great charity of will to come together in one. Behold, it says, how good and pleasant it is that brothers inhabit in one!

bible_refs.note: Ecce, quam bonum et voluptabile est ut habitent fratres in unum
In novissimis diebus manifestus mons Domini et domus Dei super vertices montium

pass_b_english: Firmilianus greets his brother Cyprian in the Lord. We have received the letters you sent us through our most beloved deacon Rogatianus, and we have given the greatest thanks to the Lord because, though we are separated in body, we have been united in spirit, as if we shared not merely one region but inhabited the very same house at the same time. That is fitting to say, because the spiritual house of God is one. For in the last days, says the Prophet, the mountain of the Lord and the house of God will be manifest above the tops of the mountains (Isaiah 2:2-3). Into it they are gathered with joy, just as this Psalm asks of the Lord, to inhabit the house of God through all the days of life (Psalm 133:1). So also in another place it has been made manifest that there is among the saints a great charity of will to come together as one. Behold, how good and pleasant it is for brothers to dwell in unity (Psalm 133:1).

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required inline citations for the prophetic and psalmic allusions (Isaiah 2:2-3, Psalm 133:1) which were present in the sense of the Latin but not explicitly numbered in the source text, fulfilling the requirement to identify them. Pass A preserves the clause structure and sense of the Latin.
